subject: Intermittent API sessions: ECMP path divergence + security-group state drops
messages:
From: James Lee <james.lee@lakeviewhealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 502s from API region-us-west-2 (seen since 03/26)

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing intermittent 502/connection resets from our services calling Redwood in us-west-2 yesterday afternoon (approx 15:00 PST). Errors are short bursts (a few seconds) but affect multiple clients behind our internal LB. Our ops team captured a short pcap and a tcpdump showing SYN/ACKs followed by RSTs when flows traverse your edge. We've attached the pcap and a screenshot of the downstream healthcheck failures.

Key observations:
- Client->Redwood request succeeds, server response starts but client receives RST and session drops.
- Problem only happens when we route through our physical edge -> ISP -> your peering (seems fine when we route through a different POP).
- We suspect path asymmetry or NAT state loss at one of the hops.

Can you confirm whether there were any config changes in your on-prem edge or BGP session flaps?

Thanks,
James
Lakeview Health — Platform Ops

Hi James,

Thanks for the quick report and the pcap — we've pulled it into the incident. I'm escalating this to networking and on-prem infra for immediate triage. Initial checks: no scheduled config pushes in us-west-2, but our edge ASRs did log intermittent BGP updates around 14:58 PDT yesterday which could change ECMP next-hops.

Rishi / Mina — can you take a look at the attached pcap and the BGP show? Main hypothesis is ECMP hash instability across our two fabric devices causing return packets to take a different path (different NAT/conntrack), which would drop state for the response and produce RSTs. If that's the case, possible mitigations: disable ECMP multipath for the affected prefix, enforce source-based hashing, or push route-change dampening. Also want to confirm whether any security-group rules with connection tracking timeouts are being hit.

I'll keep James in the loop and coordinate quick remediation if we identify a single hop.

- Vanessa
Site Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Lee <james.lee@lakeviewhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 08:22:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s from API region-us-west-2 (seen since 03/26)

Quick summary of what I pulled from the devices and the pcap attached:
- Edge ASR-1 and ASR-2 both have the same prefix for Lakeview's transit. BGP flaps observed 2027-03-26T21:58:12Z (neighbor 10.1.1.2 resets), followed by route churn for the /24.
- The pcap shows the client SYN reaching our edge, SYN/ACK from Redwood server returns, but the client receives an RST. Following flowtrace shows the TCP sequence reset occurs when the response traverses a different NAT device (NAT translation ID differs).
- ECMP group on our fabric uses a 5-tuple hash, but our downstream NAT appliances are using a different hashing seed/version after the BGP updates, causing inconsistent flow affinity during the churn window.

Attached: edge-bgp-show.txt (BGP change timestamps), lakeview_api_conntrace.pcap (filtered), and an annotated trace image.

Recommended immediate remediation (low-risk):
1) Temporarily pin Lakeview prefix to a single preferred next-hop on the affected ASR (ASR-1) to restore stable forwarding affinity.
2) Coordinate with Lakeview to confirm they don't have asymmetric source NAT on their side.
3) Post-mitigation: align ECMP hash seeds across NAT devices and enable persistent-hash (hardware feature) or source-IP affinity for customer prefixes.

Jonas — can you prepare the device commands and run the pin (we should be able to flip back in a maintenance window). I'll own the coordination with Lakeview for verification.

- Rishi
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Lee <james.lee@lakeviewhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:40:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s from API region-us-west-2 (seen since 03/26)

I executed the temporary pin at 09:10 PDT on ASR-1 to force Lakeview traffic via NextHop A (commands and change log attached to the ops record). After pinning, James reported reduced errors within ~90s and we saw no RSTs in a 20-minute observation window.

Notes from the change:
- Command run (ASR-1): ip route <lakeview-prefix> null 255.255.255.0 next-hop <NextHop A> permanent; remove from ECMP group.
- No downstream health impacts observed; we kept maintenance-party window minimal.
- Captured a follow-up pcap showing symmetric pathing and preserved NAT translation IDs.

Next steps:
- Schedule a config alignment task: synchronize ECMP hash seeds across NAT appliances and enable persistent-hash on the fabric.
- Review security-group conntrack timeouts for long-lived healthchecks (increase timeout where safe).
- Work with Lakeview to ensure their own transit doesn't reintroduce asymmetry (source NAT changes).

I'll file the change notes and hand this to the Platform Reliability team for the postmortem.

- Jonas
Network Operations, Redwood Inference
